title: Harnesses in AI: A Deep Dive — Tejas Kumar, IBM
talk_summary: Tejas Kumar defines an agent harness as everything around the model that grounds it in reality: tool registry, context management, guardrails, agent loop, and a deterministic verify step. Through a live demo he shows that adding guardrails, a deterministic verify function, and a harness-level login handler makes a weak model (GPT-3.5) complete a browser task without touching the prompt.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic verify step in the harness
takeaways.what_they_do: After each agent attempt, a hand-written deterministic function inspects the tool-call trace and returns pass/fail, instead of trusting the model's claim of success.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have this function called verify successful upvote. I wrote this. This is deterministic.

takeaways.technique: Harness-level retry loop with max attempts
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap the single agent attempt in an outer loop that retries up to N times, with max-iterations and max-messages guardrails enforced at the harness level rather than inside the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our main run harness is just a loop that runs no more than three times

takeaways.technique: Naive context compressor as a guardrail
takeaways.what_they_do: When message count exceeds a threshold, trim history to keep system prompt, user task, and last two messages only.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the guardrail is triggered, we always remove everything after the system prompt and the user prompt in the middle, and we keep the last two messages

takeaways.what_they_do: A login handler runs just before each trace push; if the browser is on a login page it injects credentials from the harness (which has secret access) and submits, then notifies the agent it logged in.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we fill in credentials and submit the button programmatically from the harness, not from the agent, deterministically and securely

takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately use an old/cheap model (GPT-3.5) and compensate with harness engineering rather than prompt changes or a bigger model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Use like Quinn or something, or even something smaller. Use GPT-OSS. It's free. And with a great harness, you can go very far.

takeaways.technique: Fix behavior in harness code, not prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Solve agent failures by adding deterministic harness logic (verify, login handler, guardrails) while leaving the prompt untouched throughout the demo.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It should not be lost on you that I did not touch the prompt once.
